newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Chile's Codelco explores in Argentina, Bolivia, Peru.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Codelco explores in Argentina, Bolivia, Peru.

text.p: Chilean state mining company Codelco, the world's biggest copper producer, is looking for exploration opportunities in Argentina, Bolivia and Peru, a senior company official said Thursday.

Codelco's Assistant Manager of International Explorations, Carlos Munchmeyer, told Reuters the most advanced search was in Argentina, where the company "is at a phase of basic exploration and carrying out studies to find new sites."
Munchmeyer was visiting Ecuador with a Codelco delegation to discuss possible mining investments with the government.

"Ecuador has an interesting potential for gold and copper. But at this moment it is premature to talk of exploration, we want to visualize the potential of the country and familiarize ourselves with the geology," Munchmeyer said in an interview.
Ecuador produced 499,035 ounces of gold in 1995 and 418,006 in 1994. The country's Undersecretary of Mining Arnoldo Alencastro told reporters Ecuador was eager to "strengthen its links with Codelco."

Munchmeyer forecast that Codelco's overall sales would be lower this year than 1995's $3.3 billion "because the price of copper is falling." Codelco hopes its biggest current project, the Radomiro copper mine, will produce 200,000 tonnes of copper by the end of 1998, for an investment of $650 million.
